rules.title: Rolling 12-month absences
rules.text: The 180-day limit applies to any 12-month period, not calendar years. Use our [absence calculator](/absence-calculator/) to check yours.

rules.title: The rules are changing
rules.text: The government plans to move most routes to a 10-year qualifying period under “earned settlement”, laid from December 2026 and coming in during 2027. The rules that apply are those in force when your application is decided. [Read about the ILR changes](/ilr-changes-2026/)

rules.title: Apply on time
rules.text: You can usually apply up to 28 days before you complete your qualifying period. Applying too early is a common reason for refusal.

rules.title: After ILR
rules.text: Most people can apply for [British citizenship](/british-citizenship/) after holding ILR for 12 months, or straight away if married to a British citizen.

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: Who qualifies for Indefinite Leave to Remain now?
sections.text: Most people apply after 5 continuous years on a route that leads to settlement, such as the Skilled Worker or spouse route. People who have lived in the UK lawfully for 10 years may qualify on the long residence route. If you already qualify, or will soon, applying before the new rules take effect is usually the safest option.

sections.heading: Time abroad and Indefinite Leave to Remain
sections.text: For most routes you must not have spent more than 180 days outside the UK in any 12-month period during your qualifying time. This is counted on a rolling basis. Some absences, such as for serious illness, can be treated differently with evidence. Use the calculator on this page to check your trips.

faqs.q: How long do I need to wait for Indefinite Leave to Remain?
faqs.a: Most routes currently need 5 years. Under the government’s plans, most routes will move to 10 years during 2027, with shorter routes for some groups.

faqs.q: How many days can I spend outside the UK for ILR?
faqs.a: For most routes, no more than 180 days in any rolling 12-month period during your qualifying time.

faqs.q: Do I need the Life in the UK test for ILR?
faqs.a: Most applicants aged 18 to 64 do. [Read our guide](/life-in-the-uk-test/).
